source_documents.title: PET-modulated fluorescence enhancement of cabergoline: A DFT and time-resolved fluorescence guided analytical strategy

reference_evidence_units.quote: The fluorescence emission of CG is not strong in its native state due to a PET process originating from its electron-donating amine group.
reference_evidence_units.subject: cabergoline
reference_evidence_units.statement: Native cabergoline is weakly fluorescent because of PET from its amine.

reference_evidence_units.quote: This lifetime extension strongly supports suppression of the PET-mediated quenching process.
reference_evidence_units.subject: cabergoline vs acidified
reference_evidence_units.statement: Average lifetime rises from 3.5 to 4.9 ns on acidification.

reference_evidence_units.quote: While the reduced HOMO-LUMO energy gap suggests a change in the electronic excitation energy, the significant enhancement in fluorescence intensity is primarily attributed to the suppression of non-radiative decay pathways.
reference_evidence_units.subject: cabergoline vs protonated
reference_evidence_units.statement: The intensity gain on protonation is assigned to removal of a nonradiative (PET) channel, not to the gap change.

reference_evidence_units.quote: explains the inability of the protonated amine to donate electrons to the excited fluorophore, thereby suppressing the PET quenching pathway.
reference_evidence_units.subject: protonated cabergoline
reference_evidence_units.statement: Protonation removes the electron density on both tertiary amine nitrogens.

reference_evidence_units.quote: partial protonation oc curs within this pH window, which likely precluded the full suppression of the PET effect originating from the lone pair electrons on the amine moieties.
reference_evidence_units.subject: cabergoline
reference_evidence_units.statement: Tertiary amine pKa 6.05-6.42: full turn-on needs strong acid.

reference_mechanisms.label: PET_ET
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Paper's explanation of the weak native emission: PET from the tertiary amine lone pairs to the excited indole chromophore; acid turns it off. Support is a lifetime increase (3.5 to 4.9 ns) and ground-state DFT; no redox data or donor-free control.
